audit_metadata.platform: StrataNoble SaaS Platform (Website + ACHIEVERY Platform + Mobile)
audit_metadata.scope: Production readiness verification with focus on previously identified vulnerabilities

blocking_issues: Production secrets committed to Git repository (.env.production)
CSRF protection disabled in development environment
Missing authentication on critical API endpoints
Row Level Security disabled on leads table
TypeScript build errors ignored in production builds
Console logging exposing sensitive data in production
Service role key potentially exposed to client-side

vulnerabilities.title: Production Secrets Committed to Git Repository
vulnerabilities.description: The .env.production file containing live Stripe secret keys, webhook secrets, and Supabase service role keys is tracked in Git and committed to the repository.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete compromise of payment processing, database access, and user data. Attackers with repository access can steal all customer payment information, access all database records, and impersonate any user.

immediate_actions: IMMEDIATELY rotate ALL exposed credentials (Stripe keys, Supabase keys, webhook secrets)
Remove .env.production from Git: git rm --cached .env.production
Add .env.production to .gitignore
Rewrite Git history to remove all traces: git filter-branch or BFG Repo-Cleaner
Audit repository access logs for unauthorized access
Notify security team and affected stakeholders
preventive_measures: Use environment-specific secret management (AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault)
Implement pre-commit hooks to prevent secret commits (e.g., git-secrets, detect-secrets)
Use .env.example files with placeholder values only
Configure CI/CD to inject secrets at deployment time

vulnerabilities.title: CSRF Protection Disabled
vulnerabilities.description: Cross-Site Request Forgery protection is explicitly disabled in the development environment, and this configuration may propagate to production.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-352: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
vulnerabilities.impact: Attackers can force authenticated users to perform unwanted actions (payment processing, data modification, account changes) without their knowledge. Critical for applications handling financial transactions.

immediate_actions: Remove SKIP_CSRF_PROTECTION from all environments
Implement proper CSRF token validation in all state-changing endpoints
Verify production environment does not have this flag set
implementation: Use Next.js built-in CSRF protection or implement custom token generation
Include CSRF tokens in all forms and AJAX requests
Validate tokens on all POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH endpoints
Use SameSite cookie attributes as additional defense

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authentication on Reframe API Endpoint
vulnerabilities.description: The /api/reframe endpoint processes user actions and updates the database without authenticating the request. User ID is client-controlled.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

evidence.vulnerability: No authentication check before processing. userId is accepted from client without validation.

vulnerabilities.impact: Attackers can reframe actions for any user, modify database records for other users, consume OpenAI API quota, and potentially inject malicious content into user data.

immediate_actions: Add validateApiAuth() call at the beginning of the POST handler
Use authenticated user ID instead of client-provided userId
Verify actionId belongs to authenticated user before updating

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Authentication on Narratives Generation API
vulnerabilities.description: The /api/narratives/generate endpoint creates and modifies weekly narrative records without authentication. Explicitly documented as 'without auth' in code comments.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function
vulnerabilities.impact: Attackers can generate narratives for any user, access other users' action data, mark actions as significant for any user, and pollute the database with fake narratives.

immediate_actions: Implement validateApiAuth() in both POST and GET handlers
Use authenticated user ID instead of client-provided userId
Add rate limiting to prevent abuse

vulnerabilities.title: Row Level Security Disabled on Leads Table
vulnerabilities.description: The leads table storing discovery form submissions has RLS commented out, allowing any authenticated user to access all lead data.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-284: Improper Access Control

evidence.current_state: RLS completely disabled with commented-out policies

vulnerabilities.impact: Any authenticated user can read, modify, or delete all lead records containing contact information, business details, and pipeline data. Complete breach of customer privacy.

immediate_actions: Enable RLS on leads table: ALTER TABLE leads ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
Create service role policy for admin access
Create restrictive policies for regular users (if needed)
Audit existing data access logs

vulnerabilities.title: Coach Dashboard Export Missing Authorization
vulnerabilities.description: The /api/coach-dashboard/export/[userId] endpoint allows exporting any user's data without verifying the requesting user has coaching permissions for that client.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

evidence.vulnerability: Authorization check documented as TODO, not implemented

vulnerabilities.impact: Any authenticated user can export comprehensive client progress reports for any user by manipulating the userId parameter. Exposes sensitive coaching data and client progress information.

immediate_actions: Implement authentication check using validateApiAuth()
Verify requesting user has coach relationship with target userId
Add permission check against coaching_relationships table

vulnerabilities.title: OpenAI API Key Exposure Risk
vulnerabilities.description: OpenAI API key is loaded in client-accessible code paths. While currently server-side only, the code structure could expose the key in client bundles.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials

evidence.risk: If these modules are imported client-side, OPENAI_API_KEY could be bundled

vulnerabilities.impact: Exposed OpenAI API key allows attackers to consume API quota, generate content on your behalf, potentially access training data, and incur significant costs.

immediate_actions: Move OpenAI client initialization to dedicated server-only files
Add 'server-only' import protection: import 'server-only' at top of files
Ensure reframe-engine.ts and narrative-engine.ts are never imported client-side
Configure Next.js webpack to exclude from client bundles

vulnerabilities.title: In-Memory Rate Limiting (Not Persistent)
vulnerabilities.description: Rate limiting implementation uses in-memory Map storage which resets on server restart and doesn't work across multiple instances.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

evidence.vulnerability: Map storage is not persistent across server restarts or horizontal scaling

vulnerabilities.impact: Rate limits can be bypassed by restarting the server or sending requests to different instances. Enables brute force attacks, API abuse, and denial of service.

immediate_actions: Implement Redis-based rate limiting with Upstash or similar
Use distributed rate limiting solution (e.g., @upstash/ratelimit)
Configure rate limits at edge/CDN level (Cloudflare, Vercel)

vulnerabilities.title: TypeScript Build Errors Ignored in Production
vulnerabilities.description: Next.js configuration explicitly ignores TypeScript errors during production builds, potentially shipping broken code.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-1104: Use of Unmaintained Third Party Components

evidence.developer_comment: Intentionally disabled 'for initial deployment' but still active

vulnerabilities.impact: Type errors and linting issues that could cause runtime failures, security vulnerabilities, or data corruption are ignored. Production code may have undefined behavior.

immediate_actions: Set ignoreBuildErrors: false
Set ignoreDuringBuilds: false
Fix all TypeScript errors before production deployment
Run `npm run type-check` and resolve all issues
long_term: Implement pre-commit hooks to prevent commits with type errors
Configure CI/CD to fail on type errors

vulnerabilities.title: Excessive Console Logging in Production Code
vulnerabilities.description: API routes contain extensive console.log, console.warn, and console.error statements that will execute in production, potentially exposing sensitive data.
vulnerabilities.owasp_category: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

evidence.example: console.error('Reframe API error:', error) - Could log user input or sensitive data

vulnerabilities.impact: Sensitive user data, API keys, error details, and system information may be logged to console/log files accessible to attackers or support staff without proper clearance.

immediate_actions: Replace all console.* calls with structured logging library (Winston, Pino)
Implement log sanitization to remove sensitive data
Configure production logging to appropriate log levels
Ensure logs don't contain PII, passwords, tokens, or API keys

vulnerabilities.title: Early Access Signups Table Writable by Authenticated Users
vulnerabilities.description: The early_access_signups table has RLS enabled but allows authenticated users to read their own records and service role has full access. No write protection for regular users.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-284: Improper Access Control

policies.authenticated: Can SELECT their own records (no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies)

evidence.vulnerability: Missing INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies means default behavior applies

vulnerabilities.impact: Without explicit INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies, table behavior depends on Supabase defaults. Users may be able to modify signup records, change status, or spam the table.

immediate_actions: Add explicit INSERT policy (anonymous users can INSERT once per email)
Add DELETE policy (only service_role can DELETE)
Add UPDATE policy (only service_role can UPDATE)
Add unique constraint enforcement at application level

vulnerabilities.title: Stripe Webhook Signature Verification Could Be Bypassed
vulnerabilities.description: Stripe webhook signature verification fails gracefully and falls back to processing if QStash is unavailable, potentially allowing unsigned webhooks in certain configurations.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

evidence.vulnerability: Fallback processing path may not verify signatures properly

vulnerabilities.impact: Attackers could send forged webhook events to manipulate subscription status, grant unauthorized access, or trigger fraudulent transactions if signature verification is bypassed.

immediate_actions: Remove fallback processing path - always require signature verification
Add redundant signature check before processing
Log all webhook verification failures for audit
Monitor for unsigned webhook attempts

vulnerabilities.title: Supabase Service Role Key Used in Client-Accessible Context
vulnerabilities.description: The supabase client in apps/platform/src/lib/supabase.ts is created with environment variables that could include the service role key if misconfigured.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials

evidence.risk: File is imported in both client and server contexts. If SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY accidentally used, it would be exposed.

vulnerabilities.impact: If service role key is accidentally used instead of anon key, client-side code would have unrestricted database access, bypassing all RLS policies and allowing complete data breach.

immediate_actions: Add explicit check to prevent service role key usage in client
Separate client and server Supabase instances
Use createBrowserClient for client-side and createServerClient for server

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Input Validation on OpenAI Prompts
vulnerabilities.description: User input is passed directly to OpenAI API without sanitization, potentially enabling prompt injection attacks.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-77: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements

evidence.vulnerability: originalText and userDream injected directly into prompt without sanitization

vulnerabilities.impact: Users could inject malicious prompts to manipulate AI responses, extract system prompts, generate inappropriate content, or bypass content filters. Could also inflate OpenAI costs.

immediate_actions: Implement input sanitization for user-provided text
Set maximum length limits on originalText and userDream
Use OpenAI's moderation API to filter harmful inputs
Escape special characters before prompt injection

vulnerabilities.title: Email Validation Regex Too Permissive
vulnerabilities.description: Trust Ledger sharing and email validation use overly simple regex that accepts invalid email formats.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation
vulnerabilities.impact: Invalid email addresses accepted for Trust Ledger sharing could cause delivery failures, data exposure to wrong recipients, or enable injection attacks through malformed email headers.

immediate_actions: Replace with RFC 5322 compliant email regex
Add DNS MX record validation for critical flows
Implement email verification for Trust Ledger shares

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy Headers on API Routes
vulnerabilities.description: Middleware sets CSP headers only for protected routes, leaving API endpoints without CSP protection.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-1021: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames

evidence.gap: API routes (starting with /api/) don't receive CSP headers

vulnerabilities.impact: API routes without CSP headers are vulnerable to clickjacking, XSS injection through API responses, and other content injection attacks.

immediate_actions: Add CSP headers to all responses, not just protected routes
Configure strict CSP for API routes
Add X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff globally

vulnerabilities.title: No API Request Size Limits
vulnerabilities.description: API endpoints do not enforce request body size limits, enabling denial of service through large payloads.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-400: Uncontrolled Resource Consumption

evidence.grep_result: No body-parser or express.json usage found in API routes
evidence.vulnerability: Next.js API routes accept unlimited request body size by default

vulnerabilities.impact: Attackers can send multi-gigabyte requests to exhaust server memory, cause crashes, or inflate storage/bandwidth costs. Particularly dangerous for /api/narratives/generate with action arrays.

immediate_actions: Configure Next.js API route body size limit in next.config.mjs
Add request size validation in API handlers
Implement request timeout limits

vulnerabilities.title: Weak UUID Validation
vulnerabilities.description: UUID validation regex does not enforce v4 UUID format, accepting potentially invalid UUIDs.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-20: Improper Input Validation

evidence.issue: Accepts UUID v1-v5, should validate v4 specifically for security tokens

vulnerabilities.impact: Accepting non-v4 UUIDs for share tokens could enable timing attacks or predictable token generation if UUID v1 (time-based) is accidentally used.

immediate_actions: Verify all generated UUIDs are v4 (random)
Consider using crypto.randomUUID() for token generation

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Data Retention Policies
vulnerabilities.description: No automated cleanup of expired Trust Ledger shares, old weekly narratives, or inactive user data.
vulnerabilities.owasp_category: A09:2021 - Security Logging and Monitoring Failures
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-1188: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default

evidence.observation: trust_ledger_shares.expires_at is checked but not enforced with cleanup
files_reviewed: supabase/migrations/*.sql - No cleanup triggers or scheduled jobs
No cron jobs or scheduled tasks for data cleanup

vulnerabilities.impact: Expired shares remain accessible, database bloat increases costs, GDPR/privacy compliance issues with retaining unnecessary user data.

immediate_actions: Create Supabase Edge Function or cron job to cleanup expired shares
Add data retention policy for weekly_narratives (e.g., keep 52 weeks)
Implement soft delete with 30-day grace period
Document data retention in privacy policy

vulnerabilities.title: Insufficient Security Headers
vulnerabilities.description: Missing Permissions-Policy and Strict-Transport-Security headers in middleware configuration.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-16: Configuration
vulnerabilities.impact: Without HSTS, users vulnerable to downgrade attacks. Without Permissions-Policy, unnecessary browser features enabled increasing attack surface.

immediate_actions: Add Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload
Add Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()
Submit domain to HSTS preload list

vulnerabilities.title: Development Secrets in Production Environment File
vulnerabilities.description: The .env.production file contains placeholder values for some services (SendGrid) indicating incomplete production configuration.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-1188: Initialization of a Resource with an Insecure Default
vulnerabilities.impact: Email functionality will fail in production. Error handling may expose placeholder values in logs or error messages.

immediate_actions: Replace all placeholder values with actual production credentials
Verify email functionality works in production environment
Add environment variable validation on startup

vulnerabilities.title: Missing CORS Configuration
vulnerabilities.description: No explicit CORS configuration found in middleware or API routes, relying on Next.js defaults.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-942: Overly Permissive Cross-domain Whitelist

evidence.grep_result: No Access-Control-Allow or CORS configuration found

vulnerabilities.impact: If CORS is later enabled without proper configuration, could allow unauthorized cross-origin requests from malicious sites.

immediate_actions: Document CORS policy in security documentation
Add explicit CORS headers in middleware if cross-origin access needed
Implement origin whitelist if API must be public

vulnerabilities.title: Overly Permissive CSP for Script Sources
vulnerabilities.description: Content Security Policy allows 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' for scripts, weakening XSS protection.
vulnerabilities.cwe_id: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation

evidence.weakness: unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval defeat CSP XSS protection

vulnerabilities.impact: Weakened CSP allows inline scripts and eval(), reducing protection against XSS attacks. Attackers can inject malicious scripts if they find injection points.

immediate_actions: Remove 'unsafe-inline' and 'unsafe-eval' from CSP
Use nonce-based CSP for necessary inline scripts
Move all inline scripts to external files
Use hash-based CSP for static inline scripts

scenario_1_complete_takeover.name: Complete Platform Takeover via Exposed Secrets
steps: 2. Extracts Stripe live secret key and Supabase service role key
3. Uses Stripe key to process fraudulent transactions
4. Uses Supabase service role key to bypass all RLS
5. Extracts all user data, payment information, and credentials
6. Modifies subscription tiers to grant free access
7. Deletes audit logs to cover tracks
scenario_1_complete_takeover.impact: Total platform compromise, financial fraud, data breach, regulatory penalties
scenario_1_complete_takeover.blocked_by: VULN-001 fix (credential rotation and Git removal)

scenario_2_unauthorized_data_access.name: Cross-User Data Access via Missing Authentication
steps: 1. Attacker creates free account on platform
5. Receives all user actions, dreams, and progress data
7. Exports comprehensive client reports for competitive intelligence
scenario_2_unauthorized_data_access.impact: Privacy breach, competitive intelligence theft, GDPR violation

scenario_3_payment_fraud.name: Webhook Forgery for Subscription Manipulation
steps: 2. If signature verification can be bypassed, crafts fake webhook
4. Grants themselves enterprise tier without payment
scenario_3_payment_fraud.impact: Revenue loss, unauthorized feature access, fraud

production_deployment_blockers: DO NOT DEPLOY TO PRODUCTION until VULN-001 through VULN-005 are fully remediated
All exposed credentials must be rotated before any production deployment
Authentication must be implemented on all API endpoints
RLS must be enabled on all user data tables
security_architecture: Implement defense in depth with multiple security layers
Use principle of least privilege for all access controls
Implement security by default (secure unless explicitly opened)
Separate client and server code with strict boundaries
Use managed secret services instead of environment variables
development_practices: Implement pre-commit hooks to prevent secret commits
Require security review for all API endpoints
Enable TypeScript strict mode and fix all errors
Use structured logging with automatic PII redaction
Implement automated security testing in CI/CD pipeline
monitoring_and_response: Set up real-time alerting for authentication failures
Monitor for unusual API access patterns
Implement audit logging for all data access
Create incident response plan for security events
